name: Fen
notes: Minerotrophic groundwater-fed peatland: alkaline to neutral, sedge-dominated with brown mosses, tall herbs, willow/alder carr and tamarack. Drawn on European calcareous fens (Britain, Alps, Baltic) and N American rich fens.

canopy.name: Tamarack
canopy.source: Larix laricina, N American rich fens and swamps, deciduous conifer 5-20 m

canopy.name: Grey alder
canopy.source: Alnus incana, Eurasian and N American fen carr and stream margins, 5-15 m multi-stemmed

canopy.name: Northern white cedar
canopy.source: Thuja occidentalis, NE North American calcareous fens and cedar swamps, 8-20 m conical

shrub.name: Fen willow
shrub.source: Salix cinerea (grey willow), European fen carr and marsh margins, bushy 2-6 m

shrub.name: Shrubby cinquefoil
shrub.source: Dasiphora fruticosa, circumboreal calcareous fens, yellow-flowered shrub 0.3-1 m

shrub.name: Bog birch
shrub.source: Betula pumila, N American fens and peatlands, 1-3 m shrub birch (B. humilis in Europe)

ground.name: Saw sedge
ground.source: Cladium mariscus (great fen-sedge), dominant of European calcareous fens (Norfolk Broads), serrated leaves 1-2.5 m

ground.name: Bottle sedge
ground.source: Carex rostrata, circumboreal poor and rich fens, dominant sedge lawn 30-100 cm at water's edge

ground.name: Black bog-rush
ground.source: Schoenus nigricans, dominant tussock of calcareous fens in Britain/Ireland/continental Europe, dark flower heads 20-60 cm

ground.name: Brown moss
ground.source: Scorpidium scorpioides, characteristic brown moss carpet of rich fens across the boreal/temperate zone

ground.name: Marsh marigold
ground.source: Caltha palustris, circumboreal fens and wet meadows, glossy leaves and yellow flowers 15-50 cm

ground.name: Grass of Parnassus
ground.source: Parnassia palustris, Eurasian and N American calcareous fens, single white flower 10-30 cm

special.note: Catalogue plants (data/plants) whose band centres fall inside this biome's climate; computed, informational. Phase 6 may raise their density here so they are findable.

associations.name: Saw sedge fen
associations.where: open groundwater-fed flats with calcareous water, deep peat
associations.source: Cladium mariscus swamp (Rodwell 1995 S2; Wheeler 1980 Fenland)

associations.name: Black bog-rush rich fen
associations.where: spring-fed seepage slopes and flushes, marl, base-rich
associations.source: Schoenus nigricans calcareous mire (Rodwell 1991 M13; Ellenberg 1988 Caricion davallianae)

associations.name: Bottle sedge-brown moss poor fen
associations.where: lake margins and quaking mats, neutral peat, permanently wet
associations.source: Carex rostrata-brown moss fen (Rodwell 1991 M9; Sjors 1948)

associations.name: Tamarack-cedar rich swamp
associations.where: forested fen edge with slow groundwater flow, peat over marl
associations.source: Larix laricina-Thuja occidentalis rich conifer swamp (Curtis 1959; Kost et al. 2007 Michigan NFI)

associations.name: Grey alder-willow carr
associations.where: stream-side fen and drainage lines, wet mineral-rich peat
associations.source: Alnion glutinosae-incanae fen carr (Ellenberg 1988; Rodwell 1991 W2/W3)
